rows.title: The key choices
textRows: Six airbags are standard across the variants. The panoramic roof is available on specified trims.
Regular petrol, diesel and turbo petrol have different gearbox pairings. Compare the complete configuration before choosing.

rows.title: Wheel finishes by trim
textRows: Choosing a wheel finish depends on the trim. SX and SX Premium have diamond-cut alloys; King has a larger diamond-cut design, while both Knight versions use matte black alloys.

rows.title: Lighting by trim
textRows: At the front, E and EX use projector headlamps. The guide lists LED headlights and connected LED tail lamps from EX(O) onwards, making lighting another difference between trims.

rows.title: Driver assistance availability
textRows: King, King Knight and Lounge Edition carry the full driver-assistance suite. Their automatic versions include cruise control with stop and go; availability depends on that engine and trim combination.

rows.title: Price and exclusions
textRows: The September guide lists a starting price of ten lakh ninety thousand seven hundred rupees ex-showroom, but records a conflicting lower figure. Tax, registration and insurance are extra; confirm the current dealer quote.

rows.title: Extended warranty terms
textRows: The guide describes up to seven years of extended warranty for petrol versions only. Extended warranty and Shield of Trust packages are paid separately from the vehicle purchase.

rows.title: Your next step
textRows: Equipment, colours and specifications may change, some illustrated items can cost extra, and colour availability also varies by trim; rendered colours may differ.
Use Contact Dealer to confirm your preferred configuration, check the written specification and current availability, then arrange a test drive before deciding.
